Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. High-level summary first, then specifics and next steps.

High-level commitment (concise for procurement):
- Redwood does not use customer content to train or improve our public models unless a customer explicitly opts in.
- For hosted customers we retain short-term copies of request content and operational logs to support debugging, abuse detection, and incident response, but these copies are not included in any model training datasets.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments we provide options to disable all customer-data telemetry and apply customer-managed keying and retention.

Detailed specifics (defaults, can be contracted):
- Request content (payloads): default retention is 60 days for hosted accounts; can be shortened (we commonly contract 7 or 30 days) or disabled for Dedicated/Private.
- Request metadata (timestamps, IP ranges, non-content routing info): default retention 90 days.
- Backups / disaster recovery snapshots: encrypted backups retained up to 180 days by default; deletion requests initiate lifecycle purge that includes backup tags and retention queues (see note below).
- Cache/KV stores (inference KV caches): ephemeral by design; cached state is purged within 48 hours after session end for hosted customers unless explicitly persisted by a customer feature.

On training: we maintain a contractual "no training" guarantee that prevents any customer-provided inputs from being used in model training pipelines. Operational telemetry (e.g., anonymized performance metrics) may be aggregated across customers for product reliability; that telemetry does not include raw customer content or identifying metadata.

Deletion / attestation / evidence:
- Customers can request full-content deletion via our support portal (we'll escalate to data-ops). Typical acknowledgement: deletion job queued within 24 hours; propagation to primary storage within 72 hours; backups and longer-lived archives included in scheduled lifecycle purge (up to 30 additional days depending on the backup window).
- We can provide a signed attestation (see attached redwood_non-training_attestation.pdf) and a short DPA snippet suitable for procurement (attached).

Next steps I recommend:
1) If you need a shorter retention window, tell me the target (7 / 30 days) and whether you need us to add a clause to the DPA.
2) I can route a deletion attestation to you once procurement confirms the DPA language.

Forwarding a couple of specific technical/contractual clarifications to our privacy lead.

Laura — thanks for the clear draft. A few amendments suggested for accuracy and procurement safety:

1) Retention defaults: prefer we present canonical host defaults as 60 days (content), 90 days (metadata), 180 days (backups) — that aligns with current production settings. Offer 7/30/60 as contractable alternatives; don't commit to automatic 7 days unless included in DPA.

2) "No training" language: confirm that "we do not use customer-provided content to train our public models" is accurate. Add a parenthetical: "unless explicitly opted-in by an authorized account admin in writing." This prevents confusion about telemetry opt-ins.

3) Deletion propagation: be explicit that primary storage deletion is quick (24–72h), but backup purges occur on next backup lifecycle run (30 days typical), so final complete removal can take up to 60–90 days in some edge cases. Offer a programmatic archive tagging flow for high-sensitivity customers that accelerates backup purge.

4) Evidence & attestations: we can provide signed attestation and a timestamped audit log showing job completion and retention changes. For PHI customers we recommend using Dedicated or Private deployments and a DPA amendment that includes the no-training clause and shorter retention windows.

I'll attach a short DPA snippet and our attestation template; you can share those with Arcus. Priyom — can you help with the HubSpot record and escalate to support-left for the attestation job?

Vivek
Head of Privacy, Redwood Inference
